A man died and another sustained burn injuries after a fire broke out in the basement of a four-storey building in south-east Delhi’s Lajpat Nagar-II, police said on Thursday (November 19). The incident occurred while fire safety equipment was being installed at the premises.
The Lajpat Nagar police station received information about the fire at building number G-5 around 1.17 p.m on Wednesday (November 18). “A police constable on patrol noticed the blaze and alerted the police, following which teams reached the spot and began evacuating residents. Five fire tenders were deployed to douse the flames,” said a senior police officer.
Police said, the basement housed the office of a private company, Milana Craft Works, owned by the building owner. Two of its employees, Gaurav (24) and Prem Singh Sharma (38), were present when the fire broke out.
“Gaurav was rescued from the basement and taken to Safdarjung Hospital, where doctors declared him dead on arrival. Prem, who sustained burn injuries, is undergoing treatment in the hospital’s ICU,” the officer said.
According to a preliminary inquiry, two workers were carrying out welding work in the basement to install fire safety equipment in the presence of Gaurav and Prem.
Gaurav’s father, who arrived from Madhya Pradesh’s Gwalior after learning of the incident, alleged that his son remained trapped in the basement for nearly 40 to 45 minutes and that the workers installing the equipment fled without raising an alarm.
“They could have raised an alarm or shouted so that everyone could have taken shelter and reached safety,” he said.
He also questioned whether the basement was authorised for commercial use. Gaurav had been working at the premises for the past 10 months, his father said.
An FIR has been registered against the building owner and the contractor under Section 106(1) (causing death by a rash or negligent act) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).
“The contractor, who supplied workers for the installation, has been summoned for questioning,” the officer said.
The exact cause of the fire is yet to be ascertained, and the role of the owner, contractor and workers is being examined, police said.
In a separate incident, an 11-year-old boy died after a fire broke out at a house in north-east Delhi’s Bhagirathi Vihar, police said on Thursday (November 19). Police suspect a short circuit may have caused the blaze.
The police received information about the fire around 10.28 p.m. on November 17 and rushed the boy, who had sustained burn injuries, to Rajiv Gandhi Super Speciality Hospital, where doctors declared him dead on arrival.
Police said, proceedings under Section 194 (accidental death) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) have been initiated at Gokalpuri police station.
